intro_script: Welcome to the daily Robotics news digest for November 5th, 2026. Today we cover AGIBOT's AI breakthrough, LiberAI's new action model, and a major robot benchmark. Tune in for the latest.
outro_script: And that's all the circuits we have for today! AGIBOT's GO-3 is really booting up the AI world. Thanks for plugging in and exploring the future of robotics with me. Until tomorrow, keep building!

items.title: AGIBOT unveils GO-3 Preview and takes top spot on three embodied AI benchmarks
items.summary: AGIBOT unveiled GO-3 Preview, an embodied foundation model that supports learning across the entire lifecycle of pre-training, post-training, and post-deployment. The model achieved first-place rankings on the RoboDojo, RoboTwin, and RoboColiseum benchmarks. GO-3 Preview unifies task understanding, future-state prediction, and action generation through its embodied-native WRAM architecture. Post-training is facilitated by Genie Evolver, which uses physical robots, simulation, and world models for continuous refinement. The system incorporates Genie Master to enable robots to learn from real-world operational experience and improve their action policies autonomously.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, AGIBOT unveils GO-3 Preview and takes top spot on three embodied AI benchmarks. This report details the introduction of an embodied foundation model that has achieved first-place rankings across the RoboDojo, RoboTwin, and RoboColiseum benchmarks. The GO-3 Preview model is an embodied foundation model designed to support learning across the entire lifecycle of pre-training, post-training, and post-deployment. It utilizes an embodied-native WRAM architecture to unify task understanding, future-state prediction, and action generation. Post-training is managed by Genie Evolver, which employs physical robots, simulation, and world models for continuous refinement. The system incorporates Genie Master to allow robots to learn from operational experience and autonomously improve action policies. This development indicates significant progress in integrating real-world experience into embodied artificial intelligence systems.

items.title: LiberAI Unveils Liber-0, a World Action Model That Grounds Human Experience in Robot Action
items.summary: LiberAI introduced Liber-0, a world action model pretrained on over 2.2 million hours of human experience to enable zero-shot robot manipulation. This model combines human video, glove-recorded motion, and embodiment alignment to transfer human manipulation skills to robots. In a zero-shot evaluation of 60 GPT-6 tasks, Liber-0 achieved 36.0% overall success without task-specific robot demonstrations. The system achieves this by grounding human experience in measured motion and aligning it with the robot's body representation. Furthermore, incorporating glove recordings can reduce the need for specific robot demonstrations, potentially saving significant data collection efforts.

The system integrates human video, glove-recorded motion, and embodiment alignment to transfer human manipulation skills to robots by grounding human experience in measured motion and aligning it with the robot's body representation. In a zero-shot evaluation across sixty GPT-6 tasks, the model achieved thirty-six point zero percent overall success without requiring task-specific robot demonstrations. Incorporating glove recordings further reduces the necessity for specific robot demonstrations, which can lead to substantial savings in data collection efforts. This advancement signals a significant step toward more intuitive and generalized robotic control systems.

items.title: RoboColosseum Launches Real-World Robot AI Benchmark With Unitree Support
items.summary: RoboColosseum is an open initiative providing access to over 100 robots and 10,000 free evaluation hours for testing robot AI on physical hardware. Unitree supports this project, highlighting its G1 platform for humanoid robotics. Initial tests revealed a significant gap between partial progress and completing full humanoid tasks, with models showing only partial success on tasks like carrying objects. The initiative aims to standardize testing by using common protocols and releasing evaluation recordings for inspection. Researchers can apply for access to this infrastructure to test model performance in varied real-world settings.

items.title: Pudu Robotics unveils ‘One Brain, Multiple Embodiments’ strategy and showcases full portfolio in European first
items.summary: Pudu Robotics unveiled its "One Brain, Multiple Embodiments" strategy and full product portfolio at the European Partner Summit in Amsterdam. This strategy aims to build a shared technological foundation across various robot forms, combining reusable AI with purpose-built hardware. The portfolio spans six product lines, including service delivery, commercial cleaning, and home lawn care. Core technologies like PuduFM and PuduAgent OS enable shared AI capabilities across different robotic platforms. Pudu is focusing on expanding robotics into diverse real-world applications across Europe.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Pudu Robotics unveils a "One Brain, Multiple Embodiments" strategy and showcases its full product portfolio in Europe for the first time. This announcement details a strategy focused on establishing a shared technological foundation across diverse robot forms by combining reusable artificial intelligence with purpose-built hardware. The showcased portfolio includes six product lines encompassing service delivery, commercial cleaning, and home lawn care. Core technologies such as PuduFM and PuduAgent OS facilitate shared artificial intelligence capabilities across these distinct robotic platforms. Pudu Robotics is concentrating efforts on extending robotics into varied real-world applications throughout the European region. This development signals a potential shift toward standardized, adaptable AI solutions for physical automation deployment.

items.title: Clearing up a robot’s fuzzy memory
items.summary: A new system, UQ-DAAAM, corrects unreliable object descriptions stored in a robot's memory by incorporating uncertainty quantification. It achieves this by comparing multiple viewpoints and captions of the same object to assess the robot's confidence in its descriptions. The system refines captions by selecting additional views that reduce uncertainty, leading to more accurate memory. This process boosts confidence and improves the accuracy of object descriptions by up to five percent. Ultimately, this method enhances a robot's ability to perform complex tasks by ensuring it remembers what it has observed with greater reliability.

items.title: Agility Robotics closes SPAC merger ahead of Nasdaq debut
items.summary: Agility Robotics completed its SPAC merger and will trade on Nasdaq under the ticker AGLT. The company manufactures Digit, a bipedal humanoid already deployed in warehouse settings for clients like Amazon and Toyota. Digit 5 is in development to incorporate safety features allowing it to work near people, with initial deliveries targeted for the first half of 2027. Agility has tentative orders totaling $300 million from prospective customers, though revenue remains small relative to spending. The company employs about 500 people and is expanding its manufacturing and engineering operations.

items.title: NYU's MABEL Puts a 56-DOF Mobile Bimanual Robot on an $8,056 Open-Source Parts List
items.summary: NYU released the design for MABEL, an open-source, mobile bimanual robot with 56 degrees of freedom. The robot features two 7-DOF arms, two 17-DOF hands, and a pitching torso, with a total open-source parts list cost of $8,056. MABEL is controllable via the Apple Vision Pro and an ACT policy trained on demonstrations. The system is released under open licenses, including CAD, firmware, and simulation models. The project aims to advance humanoid robotics by combining low-cost components into a complex, teleoperated platform.

items.title: KIST’s KAPEX Humanoid Reportedly Uses Over 90% Korean-Made Core Components
items.summary: KIST's KAPEX humanoid reportedly utilizes over 90% Korean-made core components. This development is part of a collaboration with LG and other partners for commercialization. Various Korean entities are involved in different aspects of the project, including platform, AI, batteries, and manufacturing. KIST has transferred core technology to LG Electronics, with roles assigned across the partnership. The goal is to develop a domestic humanoid industry by demonstrating reliable system performance.

items.title: How GlobalLogic helped Haystack Robotics build a UV disinfection robot
items.summary: GlobalLogic and Haystack Robotics developed an autonomous mobile robot (AMR) to provide hospital-grade UV disinfection with minimal human intervention. This robot utilizes real-time perception and edge-based intelligence to navigate complex hospital environments safely. The platform was designed to be an expandable foundation, allowing for future applications beyond disinfection. The robot features two modes: autonomous navigation and a "follow me" mode for caregiver assistance. Challenges for hospital robotics include ensuring a justifiable return on investment, meeting medical compliance standards, and navigating crowded human workflows.

items.summary: The RY H6 is a compact, lightweight robotic hand designed for smaller humanoid platforms, featuring five fingers weighing 278 grams and measuring 155 millimeters. The hand is rated modestly in terms of dexterity (2 out of 5) and strength (1 out of 5), reflecting its focus on a small physical envelope. It is currently listed as in production with an advertised price of 1,300 USD. The product offers a commercially available option for teams developing smaller robotic systems.

items.title: Are Drone Ports the Next Annoying Tech Neighbor?
items.summary: Residential concerns arose when Amazon's delivery drones, specifically the large MK30 models, generated bothersome noise and flew lower than legally permitted. Residents experienced significant annoyance from the high-pitched whine of the rotors, which acoustic research indicates is more irritating than car or airplane noise. Delivery drone companies are expanding rapidly, and while they promote positive uses, communities fear corporate overreach and safety issues. Activists and local governments have responded by challenging regulations and advocating for community engagement regarding drone operations. Ongoing disputes remain concerning noise, safety, and the legal regulation of airspace above private property.

items.title: Jev with Foresight: Safe Language-Guided Autonomous Driving via a Language World Model
items.summary: The research introduces Jev-AD, which integrates Jev, a typed decision model, with a language world model for safe autonomous driving. The language world model predicts the movement of nearby vehicles over the next two seconds to generate foreseen consequences for candidate actions. This foresight allows Jev to compare potential outcomes directly rather than implicitly inferring consequences from coordinates. In simulations, this foresight significantly reduced collision rates and improved the model's ability to achieve passenger intent. Real-world testing further demonstrated that this approach lowered collision rates in actual driving scenarios.

items.title: Ctrl-F: Force as an Interface for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: Force is proposed as a natural command channel between motion imitation and object interaction, specifying both contact location and force magnitude. Ctrl-F is a hierarchical framework that augments motion tracking with an explicit 3D force command at contact points like hands or feet. This framework includes a unified controller and a high-level force planner that issues online force commands based on object state. In experiments, Ctrl-F successfully enabled humanoid robots to manipulate objects up to 20kg through dragging, pushing, and kicking. This system demonstrated the ability to adapt force commands online as external loads changed during manipulation tasks.

items.title: MESA: An Evaluation Framework for Compositional, Semantic, and Spatial Generalization in Robotics
items.summary: MESA is an evaluation framework designed to precisely measure language-conditioned policy generalization in robotics. It introduces five evaluation suites and four generalization axes: spatial configuration, object instance, object category, and subtask composition. The framework uses MESA-Gen to generate tasks and demonstrations for large-scale evaluation. Testing seven baseline methods, the strongest model achieved 52% on MESA and 49% on the BiMESA benchmark. MESA rankings align with RoboArena scores, suggesting relevance beyond simulation.

items.title: ELA: End-to-End Latent Action Policy Learning from Video Demonstrations
items.summary: ELA is an end-to-end framework designed to learn latent actions from abundant video demonstrations for robot imitation learning. It addresses limitations in prior latent-action methods by jointly optimizing a latent action model, policy, and action decoder. This approach allows policies to effectively utilize video data with minimal action-labeled demonstrations. Experiments on manipulation tasks demonstrate that ELA consistently surpasses previous latent action baselines. The framework integrates easily with existing imitation learning methods through lightweight decoders.

items.title: Contact-Implicit Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization for Dynamic Humanoid Locomotion on Parameterizable Uneven Terrain
items.summary: A trajectory planner is presented for humanoid robots to achieve dynamic motion on complex, parameterizable terrains using a contact-implicit whole-body optimization framework. This planner generates feasible movements by considering the robot's full dynamics and kinematics without requiring predefined contact sequences. A mathematical model approximates ground geometry as a smooth surface, incorporating novel contact constraints for arbitrary smooth interactions with the ground. Nonlinear programming is employed to plan motions across various terrain topologies, and high-level requirements are integrated into the cost function for dynamic trajectory generation. Feasibility tests were conducted on non-coplanar terrains in both simulation and on the ErgoCub robot.

items.title: $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ Smooth Trajectory Planning with Application to Soft Robots
items.summary: Smooth trajectory planning is crucial for high motion performance and vibration avoidance in robotics. The required smoothness level depends on the robot's degrees of freedom and system order, and this requirement may be higher for soft continuum robots than previously assumed. The paper introduces a $\mathcal{C}^\infty$-smooth trajectory generator to produce infinitely differentiable paths while respecting kinematic limits. This method generates trajectories with continuous velocity, acceleration, and higher-order derivatives. The approach is verified through simulations and hardware testing, including the case of null boundary conditions.

items.title: Correct Robots Before They Make Mistakes: Proactive Human-in-the-Loop Intervention via Preference Learning
items.summary: A framework called Proactive Human-in-the-Loop (PHIL) allows operators to intervene by previewing policy predictions and displaying trajectories in an XR interface. During intervention, rejected predictions are paired with corrective actions, and preference-based post-training steers the policy to favor these corrections. This method was evaluated on four real-world manipulation tasks using diffusion and vision-language-action policies. PHIL significantly increased success rates and demonstration budgets compared to existing methods like HG-DAgger. Policies trained with proactive corrections also exhibited fewer unnecessary recovery behaviors.

items.title: OdorSpaces: Visual-Olfactory Embodied Navigation in 3D Environments
items.summary: OdorSpaces is a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation in 3D environments. It integrates 3D odor transport and dispersion, simulated by the Fire Dynamics Simulator, into Habitat-Sim for navigation. The platform uses both visual and olfactory observations to guide agents through photorealistic indoor settings. It is benchmarked on tasks like locating invisible gas leaks and early-stage fires. A multimodal reinforcement learning policy developed for this system significantly outperforms existing baselines.

items.title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
items.summary: OUCH presents a wrist-worn device using pneumatic actuation to deliver controlled noxious mechanical stimuli for automated neurological assessment. It achieves objective, uniform, and controlled stimulation by combining pneumatic pouches, an indenter, and a compliant spacer. Experimental results showed the indenter concentrated load significantly more effectively than a commercial algometer tip. Preliminary testing indicated that the device elicited discomfort with approximately 89% less applied force than the algometer. This work establishes a foundation for objective neurological assessment through wearable haptic stimulation.

items.title: GRASP: Gradient-Guided Sampling for Contact-Rich Physics-Based Motion Retargeting
items.summary: GRASP proposes a method for physics-based motion retargeting of human demonstrations under contact dynamics. It combines sampling-based exploration with gradient-guided refinement, avoiding the need for a differentiable simulator. GRASP-TO extends tempered sequential Monte Carlo by using gradients from local quadratic cost models to guide MCMC rejuvenation. This approach scales to long demonstrations via warm-started receding-horizon planning. Experiments show accurate retargeting for dexterous hands and humanoids, achieving 92.8% success on bimanual demonstrations.
